messages:
maria: heads up — during the telemetry sprint I noticed we have three different metric/tag names for the same auth dimension across dashboards (principal_id, principal, service_id). Can we pick one before we ship the routing telemetry UI?
cheng: ugh yeah I've seen that. my vote is to standardize on `principal_id` as the canonical label (string), and add an `auth_type` tag (`api_key|service_account|oauth`) to disambiguate. low cardinality on type, high on id.
drew: +1 for `principal_id`. question: do we want `project_id` as a tag on every auth event? billing/dashboard folks want it but that could increase cardinality explosion if people pass arbitrary project ids.
leo: for routing decisions we need project-level routing tags. Could we store project_id in the metric as an optional dimension and backfill only for known tenants? e.g. provide `project_id` when present and otherwise `project_id=unknown` and rely on sampling for unknowns.
maria: the consoles team asked for metric names that read naturally in the UI. proposed metric name: `redwood.auth.request` with labels `{principal_id, auth_type, project_id, route, outcome}`. thoughts?
cheng: metric name looks fine. small nit: our ingestion backend prefers dot-separated prefixes for system metrics, agreed. One implementation caveat: `principal_id` as a free string will dominate cardinality. We should hash or truncate in long-term storage and expose a mapping service for lookups in the console.
drew: yes we should not index raw principal_id for long retention. Idea: emit `principal_hash` (sha1 truncated) in metrics and ship a separate lightweight event to logstore with full mapping when we need to show friendly names in dashboard. That keeps metrics cardinality low.
leo: +1. Also we should document retention levels: 30d full metrics with `principal_hash`, 365d aggregated (by auth_type/outcome). Add plan to Redwood docs and console tooltip.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: telemetry/metrics-naming @staging (PR #4821) — tests passed.
maria: ok action items: 1) cheng to update ingestion to accept `principal_hash` and `principal_id` only for logstore; 2) drew to add `auth_type` tag and enum mapping in the schema; 3) leo to draft dashboard tooltips & retention language; 4) we will run a canary for 48h on staging then gradual rollout. Anyone opposed?
cheng: no objections. I'll open the schema PR and include sample export format: ```json
{"metric":"redwood.auth.request","labels":{"principal_hash":"a1b2c3","auth_type":"api_key","project_id":"proj-23","route":"/v1/complete","outcome":"success"},"value":1}```
drew: will add the enum and mapping to telemetry docs. I'll also add a small note about `project_id` cardinality and the unknown-sample policy.
leo: I'll write the tooltip copy. we should also include a short blurb in the rollout notes about what to do if a customer requests full principal-level history.
maria: perfect. I'll mark this as resolved and add a follow-up in the sprint board (link: https://redwood.internal/sprints/telemetry/tasks/123). Thanks all :thumbsup:
